note: Configuration of the saved body importer (import_native_costume.gd): the native-template-v1 six-slot layout (attack2 front SPR 82-86 + ready SPR 54), Swordsman action 86 / direction 6 fixtures and the costume.json manifest shape. The code lives in art_import.gd; this file holds the job, template, slots, fixtures and labels. New art uses board_export.gd + import_slot_board.gd instead.

recipeContract.note: What a recipe module using this importer must state (art_recipe.py validates it).

legacyKey.text: r > 0.65 and b > 0.6 and g < 0.45 and r+b-2*g > 0.85 (RGB normalized 0..1)

labels.name: {character} costume on native Swordsman action
labels.legacyOperation: Resize entire board to {canvas} nearest-neighbor once, then fixed imageRect crops from sprite-slots.json. No individual resizing, recentering, source silhouette masks, warping, or ACT edits.
labels.indexedOperation: Classify every source pixel against the style palette (magenta edges unmixed), then take the majority class of each fractional block of the whole board, then fixed imageRect crops from sprite-slots.json. No individual resizing, recentering, source silhouette masks, warping, or ACT edits.
caveats: Repaint derived from original RO body references; original head, weapon and trail remain native reference artwork.
Same bitmap dimensions and ACT data preserve the template, but generated pixels can still drift inside their slots. Per-slot alpha overlap quantifies this rather than proving artistic approval.
Reconstruction through the existing local renderer, not a capture of the official game client.
labels.done: Costume imported: {slots} body bitmaps, {frames} native attack frames, ACT unchanged.
